title: U.S. Senate · New Jersey

context.text: Incumbent Cory Booker (D) ran unopposed in the June 2, 2026 Democratic primary, winning 100% of the vote (587,980 votes).
Justin Murphy won a four-way Republican primary on June 2, 2026 with 33.4% of the vote (82,272 votes), ahead of Richard Tabor (29.2%), Alex Zdan (26.8%), and Robert Lebovics (10.7%).
Cook Political Report, Decision Desk HQ, Inside Elections, and Sabato's Crystal Ball all rated the general election Solid/Safe Democratic as of September 2026.
Eduardo Castillo, who did not run in the Democratic primary, is listed by Ballotpedia as a write-in candidate carrying a Democratic Party label in the general election.

candidates.name: Cory Booker
candidates.ballotNote: Ran unopposed in the June 2 Democratic primary

positions.summary: His Senate issues page says he has led the fight to protect the Affordable Care Act and champions proposals to build on it and increase access to care.
positions.quote: he has been a leader in the fight to protect the Affordable Care Act, while also championing proposals to build upon the law, increase access to care, and lower costs

positions.summary: His Senate issues page says he introduced the Protecting National Access to Reproductive Care Act, which would affirm FDA authority over state law for FDA-approved reproductive health products, including medication abortion drugs.
His Senate issues page says he is an original cosponsor of the Green New Deal.
positions.quote: Cory is an original cosponsor of the Green New Deal

record.text: Sits on the Senate Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry (Ranking Member, Subcommittee on Commodities, Derivatives, Risk Management, and Trade), the Committee on the Judiciary (Ranking Member, Subcommittee on Antitrust, Competition Policy, and Consumer Rights), and the Committee on Foreign Relations for the 119th Congress (2025–2026).

On March 31–April 1, 2025, held the Senate floor for 25 hours and 5 minutes, breaking the record for the longest individual floor speech in Senate history (previously held by Sen. Strom Thurmond's 24-hour, 18-minute speech in 1957). The speech criticized policies of the Trump administration's first weeks in office.

With Rep. Adriano Espaillat, introduced the Community Mental Wellness Worker Training Act, which would create a competitive federal grant program to help behavioral health organizations train community mental wellness workers to expand access to culturally and linguistically responsive mental health services.

candidates.name: Justin Murphy
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2 Republican primary with 33.4% in a four-candidate field

priorities.text: Campaign platform calls for abolishing the IRS and the Internal Revenue Code and replacing them with a flat income tax of 10–12%, eliminating the capital gains tax and estate/death taxes.

Supports completing the southern border wall, securing the northern border, withholding federal aid from self-declared sanctuary cities/states, and stationing the U.S. military on the southern border.
Supports abolishing the federal Department of Education and dividing its roughly $100 billion budget among local school boards for public education funding and school-voucher programs.

positions.summary: Calls for abolishing the IRS and current tax code in favor of a flat income tax of 10–12%, and eliminating the capital gains and estate taxes entirely.
Supports completing the southern border wall, securing the northern border, expanding 287(g) state/local immigration enforcement partnerships, and stationing the U.S. military on the border.
Describes himself as pro-life, with exceptions for the life of the mother and cases of rape/incest; opposes taxpayer funding of abortion and supports parental notification requirements.
Says he will oppose any government attempt to restrict Second Amendment rights and supports Constitutional Carry.
Supports school choice and competition between schools, and would redirect federal Department of Education funding to local school boards including for voucher programs.

Says he opposes government-run healthcare, instead proposing universal Health Savings Accounts, a national health-insurance marketplace across state lines, and anti-fraud enforcement in Medicare and Medicaid.

candidates.name: Veronica Fernandez

priorities.text: Says her platform centers on electoral reform, including a constitutional amendment to overturn Citizens United v. FEC.
priorities.quote: My platform centers on electoral reform. The SCOTUS ruling on Citizens United in 2010 opened the flood gates for the "legal" corruption of our candidates, elections, and policies. I fully support a constitutional amendment to overturn Citizens United.

priorities.text: Supports Medicare for All, arguing private insurance is structurally unable to cover ongoing healthcare needs.
Supports abolishing ICE and closing immigration detention centers, and creating a fast-tracked path to citizenship for people without more than a misdemeanor conviction.

positions.summary: Supports Medicare for All and says she will sign on to S. 1506.
positions.quote: I am a FIERCE supporter of M4A and will sign on to Bernie Sander’s Bill S1506 immediately.

positions.summary: Calls for abolishing ICE immediately and replacing it with a fast-tracked path to citizenship.
positions.quote: ABOLISH immediately and replace with a vigorous and fast-tracked path to citizenship.

positions.summary: Supports passing gun control laws, citing gun deaths among children.
positions.quote: we will be able to finally protect our children with the passage of meaningful gun control laws

positions.summary: Says she will not vote to continue arming Netanyahu's government.
positions.quote: Unlike Cory Booker, I will NOT vote in any way to continue arming Netanyahu

candidates.researchNotes: Positions are from her campaign policies page and Ballotpedia. WHYY (Sept. 22, 2026) also quotes her on Israel ("I would vote to not send money to Israel") and the Iran war.

candidates.name: Joanne Kuniansky

priorities.text: Standing with workers who resist 'the bosses’ attacks on their jobs, wages and working conditions' and building unions, per her email to WHYY.

A public works program providing jobs at union-scale wages, a shorter work week with no pay cuts, and automatic cost-of-living increases in union contracts, pensions and Social Security (as described by WHYY).

positions.summary: In her 2021 official candidate statement (New Jersey governor race), called for fighting for women's right to family planning including birth control and abortion.
positions.quote: fight for the right of women to family planning, including safe and secure birth control and abortion

statements.quote: calling for an amnesty for workers in the U.S. without papers
statements.context: In an email to WHYY, per its Sept. 22, 2026 voter guide

candidates.researchNotes: No 2026 campaign website or Candidate Connection survey was found. The abortion position is from her 2021 gubernatorial candidate statement as quoted by Ballotpedia. Other statements come from her emailed answers to WHYY (Sept. 22, 2026).

candidates.name: Eduardo Castillo
candidates.ballotNote: Write-in candidate carrying a Democratic Party label; did not appear on the Democratic primary ballot

priorities.text: Supports just-cause firing protections, a $31 minimum wage indexed to inflation, at least 15 paid vacation days per year, and paid leave after miscarriage, stillbirth, or abortion.
Supports free school meals for all students, an increased child tax credit, and free childcare, pre-K, and four-year college for all.
Supports capping ATM fees at $2.00, capping credit card interest rates at 10%, and creating a public banking option.

positions.summary: In his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, listed a $31 minimum wage indexed to inflation among his key campaign messages.
In his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, listed free childcare, Pre-K and 4-year college for all among his key campaign messages.
positions.quote: Free childcare, Pre-K, and 4-year college for all

positions.summary: In his 2025 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, listed rent stabilization among his housing proposals.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions are from his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection surveys (2026 and 2025; the rent stabilization item is from the 2025 survey). No campaign website was found.

researchNotes: Cory Booker has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey and his campaign website (corybooker.com) is fundraising-only with no published issues platform, so his priorities/positions sections rely on recent official Senate actions rather than campaign statements; per the research brief his federal floor votes and FEC totals are added separately by script. Veronica Fernandez and Eduardo Castillo's entries rely entirely on their Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey responses. Joanne Kuniansky has published no detailed 2026 platform beyond her party affiliation and 2024 election result; her entry is marked minimal. Biography gaps: Eduardo Castillo and Joanne Kuniansky have very little public biographical information beyond Ballotpedia; Murphy's local-office title differs between Ballotpedia (deputy mayor) and InsiderNJ (Township Committee member), and both are given.
